findings.text: The first paragraph says what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves ("AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable"). A newcomer can answer what it is and why it matters before scrolling.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The header links to the next steps early, and the Next steps section gives concrete commands (git clone, ./setup.sh, athena ask "add a changelog") and the prerequisites. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself"

findings.text: The page explains why the Athena homepage is mostly about another project, firstmate: it is a demonstration. But a newcomer then gets about 45 claims, 12 transition cards and a glossary about firstmate's internals. That is a lot of reading before the material about Athena itself resumes in Next steps.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit"

findings.text: The features the lede sells (one model checking another's work, the cost record, the verdict, a commit traceable to the request) are never shown on the page. The study shows traceable claims, not an example request-to-commit run, so a newcomer has to take the main promise on trust.
findings.source: "It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The prerequisites are clear, but the page does not say that running Claude Code needs an account, a subscription or an API key, or what a run might cost. It also does not say whether `athena ask` must be run inside a git repository. A newcomer may get stuck at the first try.
findings.source: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code)."

findings.text: This header link is meant for the repository owner and is not explained. A newcomer may wonder whether the proposals are theirs to decide.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: These closing sections use Athena's internal terms (job, recorded boundary, studies/ folder) without explaining them, so they read as notes for the maintainer, not the reader.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: The firstmate part is carefully built for a stranger: terms are defined before they are used, the start-to-finish walk-through is short, and the page openly says where the source is silent (for example, it gives no test for "in scope"). Readers who care about firstmate are served well.
